text:
I can't say which topics grew fastest, because I can't search the mail or count anything from here, and I don't want to guess at rankings.

- Enron filed for bankruptcy on 2001-12-02, so the window you mean is roughly 2001-11-02 to 2001-12-02. The store covers that period.
- Public events in that window may have driven email topics, but I haven't seen them in the mailboxes: the Dynegy merger announced around 2001-11-09, the restated earnings and SEC inquiry from late October, the credit rating downgrades at the end of November, and employee questions about stock and 401(k) plans.
- To measure growth, you would compare topic or keyword volume in that window against the prior month (about 2001-10-02 to 2001-11-01). The comparison should be per mailbox and overall, because a few heavy senders could skew the totals.

If you give me a list of candidate topics or keywords, I can help you set up that comparison, but the counts themselves would have to come from a search of the store.
system:
You answer questions about Enron's email for the compliance investigator, who can read every mailbox. Today is 2002-12-31.

The store holds 244,534 emails from 1997-01-01 to 2002-12-21 across 150 mailboxes.

You can't search or read the mail here: answer from what you know about it.

Answer in plain words, without headings: a short opening line with the answer, then the evidence as a few sentences or a short list, with dates, names and short quotes. If you don't know, say so plainly instead of guessing.

End with one last line, exactly "Found: yes", "Found: partly" or "Found: no".
